stage1.impression: Two speakers stand on oak plinths in a fir-lined niche over a flat, empty brown floor. It reads as a hi-fi demo booth or a game-engine showroom, not a photograph of a bar. The fir is bright, even and repeated board after board. The speakers' white insides read as raw foam blocks seen through clear plastic. There is no sign of life except two cut-off objects at the bottom-left edge. A magazine would not publish this as a specific place: nothing in the frame says listening bar rather than generic audio showroom.

blocking_9: The frame must show the listening room it is meant to sell: tub chairs, oak tables and lit Orb lamps in the foreground facing the altar, and the 200 mm step. Today only fragments at the bottom-left edge show.
The speakers must be the brightest and most legible thing on the altar. Today the fir wall behind them (lum_median 83) is brighter than the right speaker (50) and the left speaker (66).

The fir cladding and the floor must read as real materials at 1:1: board-to-board variation, checks and grain on the fir, and texture or sheen on the floor instead of a flat field (floor lum p5 to p95 is 10 to 43 with no detail).
The room's orange cast must calm down so that the speakers carry the frame's colour. The cove and wall run r 112 to 121 against b 28 to 44.
The horns must read as glossy objects with defined edges, not dark smears. The right horn's lum_median is 26.
Pools of light and dark must sit between objects, with signs of life (a glass and a record on a table, a coat) inside the frame rather than cut off at its edge.

defects.what: The floor is a featureless dark brown plane: no texture, no sheen, no reflections of the plinths. It reads as a void.
Lamp and object fragments are cut off at the frame edge. The props and furniture that belong to the frame are outside it.
The fir boards repeat with near-identical grain and tone, with no checks, nail holes or end-grain variation. It reads as a tiled veneer texture.
The cove soffit has two hot spots and a saturated orange cast (r 112, b 28) that pulls the eye above the speakers.
The white batts read as near-white (lum 223) foam blocks seen through clear sheet. The smoked tint does not register.
The horn reads as a dark blob with smeared reflections (lum_median 26). Its lip and form are barely legible.
The black backing panels behind the speakers are flat, matte and unlit, like cardboard cut-outs.
The white glowing rim at the plinth top clips (0.18 %) and reads as LED strip or signage.
A pale square block stands in front of the right plinth: a sleeve against the plinth that reads as an untextured box.
The shell around the niche (concrete, beams, steel) has dropped to near black (lum_median 12). None of the shell's materials show.

changes.problem: The frame does not show what it is for: the chairs, tables, Orbs and step in front of the altar are out of shot, so it reads as a showroom niche.

evidence.measured: The lower quarter is empty floor (lum_median 24). Only chair and lamp fragments show at [0, 730, 220, 800].

change.to: position [10.6, 2.0, 1.15] (seated eye height behind the last tub chair), target [16.6, 3.05, 0.95], 32 mm, f/2.8 focused at [15.6, 3.0, 0.9]

changes.expected: Two or three tub chairs and an oak table with a lit Orb fill the lower third as dark silhouettes in pools of light, with the step edge visible. The altar sits in the upper-middle two thirds, and the shell's concrete and beams frame it at the sides.

changes.problem: The fir wall outshines the speakers, so they are not the hero.

evidence.measured: Wall lum_median 82.8. Right speaker [780, 260, 930, 550] 49.9. Left speaker [305, 270, 440, 545] 65.7.

change.setting: the altar 2 x spot; the lit niche's strip
change.to: 60.0 W, cone 12.0 deg, 2700 K, aimed at the woofers; strip 0.07

changes.expected: Each speaker sits in its own pool of light and the wall falls off behind it. The speakers reach lum_median of 70 or more, and the wall between them drops to about 50.

changes.problem: The zone's own practicals (the Orbs) give no light, so there are no pools on the tables and nothing is cosy or lived-in in the foreground.

evidence.measured: Orbs are set to 0.058 W with liner glow 0.0092. The foreground floor is lum_median 24 and flat.

changes.expected: Each Orb throws a warm pool about 600 mm across onto its oak table top and the velvet chair arms. The liners glow below clipping.

changes.problem: The room is saturated orange, so the room carries the colour instead of the products.

change.to: 2900 K (neutralising more of the tungsten warmth), AgX - Base Contrast, saturation -10 %

changes.expected: The fir reads as warm honey-brown rather than orange. The wall's b_median rises toward half its r_median.

changes.problem: The horns read as dark smudges with formless reflections.

evidence.measured: lum_median 26.2, p95 97. Reflections are blurred blobs.

change.setting: on each speaker 4 x area (the lamps on the speakers)
change.to: 1.5 W/m2 at the target, 3000 K, with one area lamp raised to graze the horn's top lip

changes.expected: Each horn shows a crisp specular line along its lip and a readable mouth. Its body reaches lum_median 40 or more without clipping.

changes.problem: The floor is a dead flat field with no material and no reflections.

evidence.measured: lum p5 to p95 is about 10 to 43. No visible texture or reflection of the plinths.

change.to: honed concrete, roughness 0.35, with aggregate and faint trowel variation

changes.expected: Soft, broken reflections of the plinth glows and the Orbs on the floor. Real texture shows at 1:1.

changes.problem: The Douglas fir cladding reads as one tiled veneer texture.

evidence.measured: Visual inspection at 1:1: near-identical boards, no checks or nail holes, and even tone from board to board.

change.to: a per-board random tone of plus or minus 12 % and a random UV offset per board, an oil finish with roughness 0.55, and a few checks and darker end grain at the joints

changes.expected: The boards vary like real reclaimed fir. No repeat is visible across the wall.

changes.problem: The pale sleeve leaning against the right plinth reads as an untextured box. The glowing plinth rims read as LED strip.

evidence.measured: The sleeve is a flat pale block. The plinth rim clips at 0.07 to 0.18 %.

change.setting: props (sleeve against a plinth); speaker lit-base level via the altar spots
change.from: a pale square sleeve facing the camera
change.to: a darker printed sleeve angled 30 deg, with a record half out on the zone table instead; lower the altar exposure on the plinth tops with spot aiming so that no rim clips

changes.expected: The prop reads as a record sleeve. The plinth rims stay below clipping.

out_of_scope.request: Make the smoked tint of the speaker cabinets read: today the white batts show at near-white (lum 223) as if through clear sheet.
out_of_scope.why: The speakers' colour and parts are fixed EARF products. If the smoked acrylic's absorption is wrong in the render material, that is a product-model fix, not a picture fix.

out_of_scope.request: Give the black backing panels behind the speakers relief or a material.
out_of_scope.why: The niche and altar design is fixed by the card.
